content: GOAL: choose one coupling position for a behaviour x hyperbolic mechanism on RQ-VAE SIDs that is not one of the rejected rounds (poincare-frechet-successor-codebook, CURVCTRL-SID = per-level curvature from prefix-transition score, BRad-RQ = entropy-ranked radial assignment, LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ, behcone-prefix-rq, succboost-geoshift, BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ, TSG-SID). READ: the task text, the scope contract and the round history supplied in the prompt (no workspace files were needed; the repository was not readable from this session). OBSERVED: every rejected idea mutates either the codebook (Frechet/EMA), the curvature per level, the radial rank of items, a successor profile, a cone, a MoE branch, or is an unspecified acronym; none of them puts a *second behavioural endpoint* inside the curved level-wise argmin, and none uses a popularity-adjusted (PMI) co-consumption graph. REASONING: to be distinct I take (a) a behaviour signal no rejected round names - symmetric, popularity-corrected co-consumption (PMI) neighbours instead of the directed successor distribution - and (b) an untouched codebook and untouched curvature, with the behaviour entering only as an extra target remainder in the level-l score, propagated by subtracting the same chosen code tangent vector so the constraint reaches every prefix level. OPEN: constant derivation (c, r_max, k, clip ratio) and the exact Poincare formulas to be written out.

GOAL: verify that every constant of the candidate mechanism is derived/documented rather than tuned, and that the three switches are part of the computation with no ablation run needed. READ: nothing external; derivation done on paper. OBSERVED: (1) curvature c=1 fixed, standard Poincare ball; (2) ball radius r_max=0.9 is the usual clamp, and the map scale is DERIVED as kappa = artanh(r_max)/(sqrt(c)*s) with s = 99th percentile of ||z|| over training items, so no free scale; (3) the two score terms carry equal weight 1 by unit symmetry (same units, same metric) - nothing to tune; (4) the anchor remainder is clipped to tangent norm <= ||r_l||, a scale-relative bound with ratio 1 (anchor term can never dominate the content term), also unit-free; (5) PMI neighbour count k=20 is a documented default (twice the Recall@10 cut-off), PMI threshold 0 fixes the neighbour set (only positive PMI), so no threshold sweep; (6) no new loss weight exists. Switches: behaviour-off sets a_l := r_l, which makes the two score terms identical and restores the pure curved RQ ordering exactly; geometry-off replaces exp/log/d_c by identity/linear/Euclidean norms. Both are read from flags at construction, no arm is trained. REASONING: the mechanism survives the binding experiment policy (one run, one seed, no sweep, no ablation arm) because the baseline behaviour is recoverable analytically by the flag, and the content-only counterfactual argmin can be LOGGED for free in the same run's diagnostic pass (no second training). OPEN: write the final block and the JSON answer.

IDEA: PMIANCHOR-CURVED-RQ
TITLE: Popularity-adjusted neighbour anchors steer a curved RQ-VAE residual: a behaviour-conditioned Poincare code selection that constrains every SID prefix level
MOTIVATION: Content-only RQ-VAE Semantic IDs place items that play the same behavioural role in different prefix subtrees, because a co-consumed complement and its partner usually look nothing alike. The Stage-3 generative recommender then has to learn the same next-prefix distribution once per subtree, and adjacent prefixes compete; recall saturates. The target is Stage-3 test_recall@10 above 0.065, obtained by making the prefix hierarchy partially role-aware without giving up content decidability.
NOVELTY: Nothing in the codebook and nothing in the curvature is changed: no Frechet/Einstein codebook update, no per-level curvature control, no radial or rank modulation, no successor-profile smoothing, no cones, no mixture-of-branches. The behaviour signal is a symmetric popularity-corrected (PMI) co-consumption graph, not the directed successor distribution used by the earlier rounds. It enters as a SECOND GEODESIC ENDPOINT inside the level-wise argmin: each level compares the code to the current content remainder and to the current behaviour-anchor remainder in the same Poincare metric, and the anchor remainder is propagated with the same chosen code vector so the constraint is active at levels 1..L, not at one level.
CHANGE: The residual chain is redefined in the tangent chart at the ball origin, the level-l code is chosen by a two-term Poincare score (distance from the content remainder point plus distance from the clipped behaviour-anchor remainder point), and the reconstruction loss becomes the Poincare distance to the exponential image of the sum of chosen code tangent vectors.
SPECIFICATION: Frozen item embeddings z_i (N=24556 train items, dim d). Scale kappa = artanh(r_max)/(sqrt(c)*s), s = 99th percentile of ||z_i||, r_max=0.9, c=1. Item point p_i = exp_0(kappa*z_i), so its tangent vector is r_1^i = kappa*z_i. Training-session co-occurrence gives PMI neighbours j of i (only PMI_ij>0, top k=20) with weights w_ij = PMI_ij / sum_j PMI_ij; the behaviour anchor is the closed-form Einstein midpoint a_i = sum_j w_ij*gamma_j*p_j / ||sum_j w_ij*gamma_j*p_j|| with gamma_j = 1/(1-c||p_j||^2), and a_1^i = log_0(a_i). Greedy loop l=1..L: clip atilde = a_l * min(1, ||r_l||/||a_l||); score_k = d_c(exp_0(r_l), e_{l,k})^2 + d_c(exp_0(atilde), e_{l,k})^2; take the argmin code, set SID_i[l]=k, u = u_{l,k} = log_0(e_{l,k}), then r_{l+1} = r_l - u and a_{l+1} = a_l - u. Loss = d_c(p_i, exp_0(sum_l u_{l,c_l}))^2 + commitment; codebook updated exactly as the baseline. Weights are 1:1 by unit symmetry, the clip ratio is 1, k=20 is a documented default (twice the Recall@10 cut-off) and only positive PMI is admitted, so no constant is swept.
COST: Per step, 2*L*K*B = 2*3*256*1024 = 1.57M curved distance evaluations (about 40 MFLOP plus ~5M tanh/artanh) against a transformer step of order 1e11 FLOP: expected below 3% step time, below 2% wall-clock over 3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72000 steps. Plus B*L = 3072 exp_0/log_0 evaluations per step. One-off preprocessing on CPU: sparse session co-occurrence over 24556 items (10^5-10^6 pair increments), top-20 lists about 4 MB, anchors N*d floats, zero recurring cost because training-split transitions are fixed.
HYPOTHESIS: If SID prefixes carry behavioural role, then items that are far more co-consumed than popularity predicts wi

ll share level-1 and level-2 prefixes far more often than content-only assignment allows, level-2/3 prefix conditional entropy on training sequences will fall, and Stage-3 test_recall@10 will exceed 0.065 in the single frozen run. It is worthless if recall stays at or below 0.065 while the logged steering rate (fraction of items whose chosen code differs from the content-only argmin) is above 5% and the PMI prefix share rose, or if the steering rate is near zero, in which case the coupling is inert.
RISKS: Behaviour anchors could drag items into codes that no longer decode their content, raising reconstruction error and making the SID ambiguous for the recommender; chain-like catalogues could compress into shared level-1 codes and inflate collisions; the PMI graph on long sessions may be noisy for cold or rare items; the discrete argmin gives no direct gradient, so the encoder only feels the behaviour through the reconstruction of the newly chosen code; a single seed may not distinguish a small gain from noise.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Popularity-adjusted co-consumption neighbours of each item (positive-PMI top-20) with their PMI weights, condensed into one Einstein-midpoint anchor per item.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the training split only: take every training user sequence, deduplicate items per sequence, increment item counts n_i and unordered pair counts n_ij; p_ij propto n_ij, p_i propto n_i; PMI_ij = log(p_ij/(p_i*p_j)); keep j with PMI_ij>0, top 20 by PMI; normalize w_ij proportional to PMI_ij. Computed once before Stage 2, stored as a frozen buffer.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: The PMI graph, the anchor tensor, the scale s and the clipping ratio are all computed from training-split sequences and training-item embeddings before Stage 2 and stored read-only; validation and test interactions never enter the counts, the anchors or the SID construction, and no Stage-2 checkpoint selection, early stopping or Stage-3 tuning touches them. Hyperparameters are fixed in advance of the run.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Poincare ball with fixed negative curvature c=1: exponential and logarithmic maps at the origin, exp_0(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)||v||)*v/(sqrt(c)||v||), log_0(p) = artanh(sqrt(c)||p||)*p/(sqrt(c)||p||), and the Moebius distance d_c(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c))*artanh(sqrt(c)||(-x) xor_c y||); the Einstein midpoint supplies the anchor.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside the RQ-VAE quantization during Stage-2 training: the level-wise code selection, the residual recursion and the reconstruction term; the codebook entries themselves stay as points of the ball (tangent chart at the origin), unchanged in number and update rule.
COUPLING PATH: One loop per item: content remainder r_l and behaviour-anchor remainder a_l are both exp-mapped into the ball, both compared to the SAME candidate code with the SAME curved metric, the winning code updates both remainders, so the code chosen at level l depends on the behaviour anchor computed from the PMI graph and on the curvature, and removing either change does change the sequence of codes.
COUPLING EQUATION: score_l(k) = d_c(exp_0^c(r_l^i), e_{l,k})^2 + d_c(exp_0^c(atilde_l^i), e_{l,k})^2 with atilde_l^i = a_l^i * min(1, ||r_l^i||/||a_l^i||), r_{l+1} = r_l - u_{l,c_l}, a_{l+1} = a_l - u_{l,c_l}, a_1 = log_0^c( EinsteinMidpoint{ w_ij, p_j } ), u_{l,k} = log_0^c(e_{l,k}).
OBSERVABLES: steering rate per level (share of items whose chosen code differs from the content-only argmin, logged in the same run); PMI-neighbour prefix share at level 1

and level 2 of the produced SIDs; per-level code usage entropy; level-2 and level-3 prefix conditional entropy measured on training sequences; reconstruction Poincare error; Stage-3 test_recall@10 (the judgement).
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: Flag behaviour_anchor=False sets atilde_l := r_l for every level, so the two score terms coincide, the argmin equals the pure curved RQ ordering and the mechanism reduces to the curved baseline; the flag exists and is exercised in a unit test on a fixed batch, but no such arm is trained.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: Flag hyperbolic=False replaces exp_0/log_0/d_c with identity maps and Euclidean norms: score_l(k) = ||r_l - e_{l,k}||^2 + ||atilde_l - e_{l,k}||^2, the anchor is the weighted Euclidean mean of neighbour embeddings, and the reconstruction is a squared Euclidean error; exists, never trained.
ABLATION BOTH ON: The full coupled run: PMI anchors active and Poincare metric active at every level, which is the single trained candidate.
SPEC EQUATIONS: p_i = exp_0(kappa z_i), kappa = artanh(0.9)/s, s = q99(||z||); gamma_j = 1/(1-||p_j||^2); a_i = (sum_j w_ij gamma_j p_j)/||sum_j w_ij gamma_j p_j||, w_ij proportional to max(PMI_ij,0) over top-20; a_1 = log_0(a_i); for l in 1..L: atilde = a_l * min(1, ||r_l||/max(||a_l||,1e-8)); s_k = d_c(exp_0(r_l), e_{l,k})^2 + d_c(exp_0(atilde), e_{l,k})^2; c_l = argmin_k s_k (lowest index on ties); SID_i[l]=c_l; u = log_0(e_{l,c_l}); r <- r-u; a <- a-u; loss = mean_i d_c(p_i, exp_0(sum_l u_{l,c_l}))^2 + beta*mean_i ||r_1^i - sg(sum_l u_{l,c_l})||^2 with beta as in the baseline.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: frozen training-item content embeddings z_i, training-split SID-construction session sequences (for the PMI graph), codebook of L levels x K codes as ball points, flags behaviour_anchor and hyperbolic. Outputs: one SID tuple (c_1..c_L) per item, the curved reconstruction loss and gradients for encoder and codebook, and a diagnostics record with steering rates, PMI prefix shares, usage entropy and per-level prefix entropy.
SAFEGUARDS: clamp ||p|| <= 0.9 and the artanh argument to 1-1e-7; eps=1e-8 in the clip-ratio denominator and in every norm; if the Einstein-midpoint numerator has norm below eps or the item has no positive-PMI neighbour, set a_1 := r_1 so the anchor term duplicates the content term and the baseline ordering is exactly preserved; the anchor tensor is a detached frozen buffer so no gradient forces the encoder to satisfy behaviour; deterministic tie-break by lowest code index; no codebook reinitialisation or usage-weight sweep is added; all diagnostics are recorded only and never gate the run.
END IDEA
